record.original_question: For the same endpoint-map setting in sub-Riemannian geometry, can length-minimizing singular curves issuing from a fixed point q0 fill a subset of M of positive measure, or is their image always measure-theoretically small?

evidence.quote: An important open question: can they fill a positive measure subset of M?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth connected manifold equipped with a sub-Riemannian structure: a smooth bracket-generating distribution $\Delta \subset TM$ together with a smooth fiberwise inner product on $\Delta$. An absolutely continuous curve $\gamma:[0,1]\to M$ is called horizontal if $\dot\gamma(t)\in\Delta_{\gamma(t)}$ for almost every $t$, and its length is $\ell(\gamma)=\int_0^1 \lVert\dot\gamma(t)\rVert\,dt$. Fix a point $q_0\in M$ and consider the endpoint map $\mathrm{End}_{q_0}:\Omega_{q_0}\to M$, $\gamma\mapsto\gamma(1)$, defined on the Hilbert manifold $\Omega_{q_0}$ of horizontal curves issuing from $q_0$ with square-integrable controls. A horizontal curve $\gamma\in\Omega_{q_0}$ is called singular (or abnormal) if $\mathrm{End}_{q_0}$ fails to be a submersion at $\gamma$. A horizontal curve is length-minimizing if its length equals the sub-Riemannian distance between its endpoints.

Let
$$S(q_0) \;=\; \bigl\{\gamma(1) : \gamma\in\Omega_{q_0}\text{ is singular and length-minimizing}\bigr\}\subset M.$$

Question: Does there exist a sub-Riemannian manifold $(M,\Delta,g)$ and a point $q_0\in M$ such that $S(q_0)$ has positive Lebesgue (volume) measure in $M$, or is $S(q_0)$ always a measure-zero subset of $M$?
artifact.status_search_result: This question is a form of the (minimizing) Sard conjecture in sub-Riemannian geometry. It remains open in full generality. The strongest known result, established for analytic rank-2 distributions on 3-dimensional analytic manifolds, shows that the set reached from $q_0$ by singular horizontal paths has Hausdorff dimension at most 1, in particular Lebesgue measure zero. Recent work on subdifferentials and the minimizing Sard conjecture provides further partial results, but the general case is still open.

status_evidence.title: Strong Sard conjecture and regularity of singular minimizing geodesics for analytic sub-Riemannian structures in dimension 3
status_evidence.snippet: For totally nonholonomic analytic distributions of rank 2 on 3-dimensional analytic manifolds, the set of points reachable by singular horizontal paths from a given point has Hausdorff dimension at most 1.
status_evidence.claim: The Sard-type question is resolved (negatively, i.e. measure zero) in the analytic 3-dimensional rank-2 case.

status_evidence.title: Subdifferentials and minimizing Sard conjecture in sub-Riemannian geometry
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the minimizing Sard conjecture, which addresses the size of the set of endpoints of singular minimizing horizontal curves.
status_evidence.claim: The minimizing Sard conjecture remains an active open problem with partial progress.
